title: Bankruptcy Prediction Using Extreme Class Imbalance Data: Comparing Different Machine Learning Methods
authors: Chen, Y.; Wu, X.; Zhang, L.
tldr: Cost-sensitive Random Forest with missing value indicators achieves the best bankruptcy prediction performance (AUC 0.9597), capturing over 60% of bankruptcies when reviewing only the top 5% of firms.
problem_and_motivation: Bankruptcy prediction is crucial for financial risk management, but real-world datasets exhibit extreme class imbalance with far more healthy firms than bankrupt ones. Traditional metrics are misleading for imbalanced data, and existing methods often fail to capture the complex nonlinear relationships between financial features and bankruptcy risk.
approach: Used Polish Company Bankruptcy Dataset from UCI Machine Learning Repository (2023 version) with 10,503 firms, 64 financial features, and 5-year observation periods.
Applied six methods: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Artificial Neural Network, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and XGBoost.
Implemented four data preprocessing strategies: oversampling, undersampling, combined (SMOTE + Tomek), and feature engineering with missing value indicators.
Evaluated models using recall, precision, AUC-ROC, and F1-score to address extreme class imbalance (5.3% bankruptcy rate).
Used 80%-20% stratified train-test splits with five-fold cross-validation.
Engineered missing value indicators to capture information about missing values in financial statements.
findings: Random Forest with missing value indicators achieves best AUC-ROC (0.9597) and recall (0.7691) for bankruptcy prediction.
XGBoost performs best without missing value indicators (AUC 0.9487), but Random Forest surpasses it when indicators are added.
Combined preprocessing (SMOTE + Tomek) consistently outperforms oversampling or undersampling alone across all models.
Missing value indicators improve performance across all models: Random Forest recall improves from 0.4207 to 0.7691.
With cost-sensitive Random Forest, 5% of firms reviewed captures over 60% of bankruptcies (profit-based metric).
Decision Tree with combined preprocessing achieves highest F1-score (0.6433) but lowest AUC, indicating threshold-dependent performance.
Standard metrics (accuracy) are misleading for imbalanced data: all models achieve >90% accuracy regardless of actual predictive power.
Random Forest outperforms individual classifiers due to ensemble averaging reducing variance and handling nonlinear relationships.

key_equations.explanation: Area Under ROC Curve measuring model ability to distinguish classes across all thresholds, robust to class imbalance.
Profit-based evaluation metric measuring percentage of bankruptcies captured within the top-ranked firms.
Cost-sensitive cross-entropy loss assigning higher weights to minority class (bankrupt) examples.

definitions.definition: Dataset condition where one class (bankrupt firms) represents a very small fraction (5.2%) of total observations.
Machine learning approach assigning higher misclassification costs to the minority class to improve recall for rare events.
Binary features indicating whether original financial variables are missing, capturing information about reporting quality.
Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique generating synthetic minority class samples through nearest-neighbor interpolation.
Undersampling method removing majority class samples that form Tomek links with minority class samples to clean decision boundaries.
Evaluation measure capturing the percentage of actual bankruptcies found when reviewing a specified percentage of top-ranked firms.

topics.name: Clustering and Segmentation Algorithms for Transaction Data
topics.justification: The paper applies classification and ensemble methods to segment financial data into healthy vs. bankrupt categories, demonstrating feature engineering and ensemble learning approaches applicable to financial data clustering and risk segmentation.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper demonstrates that cost-sensitive Random Forest with missing value indicators achieves state-of-the-art performance for bankruptcy prediction with extreme class imbalance. It introduces a profit-based evaluation metric that is more practical than standard metrics for imbalanced classification, showing that reviewing only the top 5% of firms captures over 60% of bankruptcies. The findings have direct implications for financial risk monitoring systems.
directly_justifies: Cost-sensitive Random Forest with missing value indicators achieves 0.9597 AUC-ROC for bankruptcy prediction.
Missing value indicators improve model recall from 0.4207 to 0.7691 by capturing reporting quality information.
Combined SMOTE + Tomek preprocessing consistently outperforms single resampling methods.
Standard accuracy metrics are misleading for imbalanced financial data.
Profit-based metric demonstrates practical value: 5% review captures 60% of bankruptcies.
limits: Polish dataset may not generalize to Philippine or other developing economy financial contexts.
Financial features are limited to accounting data, excluding market sentiment and macroeconomic factors.
Static models do not capture temporal dynamics of bankruptcy risk evolution.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan of all topic domains was conducted. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) was selected as the primary match because the paper directly applies machine learning classification to predict bankruptcy risk, demonstrating ensemble learning, feature engineering, and cost-sensitive approaches applicable to financial data segmentation. No other domains match, as the paper does not address behavioral finance, budgeting systems, or real-time monitoring.

limitations: Evaluation limited to Polish company data, potentially not generalizable to other economic contexts.
Accounting-based features exclude market sentiment and macroeconomic indicators.
Static cross-sectional models do not capture temporal evolution of bankruptcy risk.
remember_this: Random Forest with missing value indicators achieves 0.9597 AUC, the best performance for bankruptcy prediction.
Missing value indicators improve recall from 42% to 77% by capturing financial reporting quality.
SMOTE + Tomek combined preprocessing outperforms single resampling methods consistently.
Standard accuracy is misleading: all models achieve >90% accuracy regardless of actual predictive power.
Cost-sensitive learning with 5% threshold captures over 60% of actual bankruptcies.
